inspection_scope: Complete supplied film plan reviewed as data: script, chapter, setup, beat contract, semantic center, visual rule, before/after state, dominant action, composition, hierarchy, environment, continuity tokens, and reset plan.

checks.evidence: Setup s1 uses one coherent physical rule: closing a route gap permits the token to cross. No unrelated mechanism is assigned to this world.
The route changes from visibly open to closed, then carries the token. No obsolete mechanism or prior state is planned to linger.
The route, bridge, gap, and token form one causal transit group rather than unrelated dominant groups.
The film contains one setup and one proposition, so there are no unrelated consecutive compositions whose staging can stagnate.
No cross-setup continuity tokens are declared. The token remains locally meaningful as the object transported within s1.
The planned environment is limited to a paper backboard, work surface, and route support; the corner crop is explicitly used to direct attention to the contact.
There is no semantic shift inside the single-proposition film. Setup s1 ends after the visible consequence, so no intermediate reset is structurally required.
The close-cropped route and token are the declared hero, focal target, and dominant action. No secondary motion, Bot, or competing active group is planned.
The central action independently expresses the claim: a visible bridge closes the route gap and the previously blocked token crosses to the other side.

setup_assessments.evidence: The entry state, bridge closure, token transit, and exit state all develop one visual rule—closed connection permits transit—with a single dominant causal action and a justified end reset.

limits: Data-only review can assess the planned structure and hierarchy but cannot establish rendered clarity, pixel visibility, mobile-glance performance, motion execution, caption synchronization, or listening quality.
